Contracts and edge cases, applied: wrote qa/test_qa.py with 15 tests. They cover path traversal, absolute names, NUL, sibling-prefix escape and inner `..`; many malformed, tampered and non-string tokens; ids that round-trip or are rejected; LIKE escaping with backslash, quotes and SQL injection; owner isolation; blank tab/newline values; and two catalogues on one connection.

gaps: The architecture says nothing about non-ASCII owners, file names or search text, so those were not tested.
`verify` accepts an empty secret, because only `issue` validates it. Section 6 does not require `verify` to reject one, so it is not reported.
No concurrency tests: sqlite3 connection sharing across threads is outside the contract.
Linux only. Windows path semantics were not tested.

My first attempt to write the test file through the shell was rejected by a hook that reported 'Contains Unicode whitespace'. I did not work around the hook. I wrote the file with the Write tool instead, and the test file contains no such characters.

advisory.problem: The brief says names come from untrusted users and the path is kept inside `base`. No test covers a name that escapes the base, such as `../x` or `/etc/passwd`. The contract line is not turned into a test.
advisory.evidence: `return os.path.join(os.path.abspath(base), name)` passes all three storage tests, and it lets `../../etc/passwd` or an absolute name escape the base.

advisory.problem: AC-006 covers only a foreign secret and three plain malformed strings. It has no tampered token, such as a changed expiry or file id with the old signature. It has no malformed string that looks like a real token but has bad encoding, such as `!!.!!`. A weak signature that leaves out the expiry would pass. A decoder that leaks `binascii.Error` or `UnicodeDecodeError` would also pass, though the criterion says no other exception may be raised.
advisory.evidence: `issue` returns `b64(id).b64(expiry).sha256(secret+id)`, so the expiry is not signed. `verify` splits on `.` and raises `InvalidToken` when the part count is not 2. This passes all four token tests, and an attacker can edit the expiry.

advisory.problem: The return value of `add` (the new row id) is never asserted, though the contract states it. `issue` is only tested with `file-42`, so a different id would not be checked.
advisory.evidence: An `add` that returns `0` or `None` passes every catalogue test.
